snippet.title: We only get this chance every 3 years…
snippet.description:
We have a chance to actually control our own devices

US Federal Register Notice: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/28/2026-21939/exemptions-to-permit-circumvention-of-access-controls-on-copyrighted-works

Every 3 years the US Library of Congress has to decide on which exemptions they'll grant for the law that prohibits bypassing copyright protection software. This is extremely important for users who want full control over their devices. Without it, it would be illegal to access our own data on many devices, fully control them, or modify them even though we physically own it. This is because of DRM which is meant to block such access or modifications, and it is literally illegal to bypass, UNLESS an exemption is made. Now it is once again time we can submit comments to the government on why they should grant certain exemptions like this.

snippet.title: The SSL and PHP Situation is Insane (and hilarious)
snippet.description:
Two insane security nightmares in one week!

This week PHP had a massive exploit released before the patch was available, effecting virtually all versions of PHP, leaving website owners scrambling. And also, a trusted root authority somehow managed to generate private keys for their intermediate certificates using all numbers less than 256, allowing them to be instantly brute forced. In fact, one of the private keys was literally the number "4'. This is actually maybe the funniest cyber-security screw up I've heard of in a while.

snippet.title: Rare W From Apple
snippet.description:
Apple managed to not do something stupid, amazing!

Apple has decided to roll back a decision they had announced in June, which would change the structure of "Hide My Email" addresses generated as part of that feature. For as long as the feature's existed, it would generate @ iCloud .com email addresses, and then that would forward to your main email. So no individual site or app would know your main email and you could track what they do with it. However, they had announced they would start putting Hide My Email addresses on a subdomain. This would make them easily identifiable, and many websites would simply block it, ruining it for many. But fortunately Apple has decided against this dumb move. I talk about why this is good, why they did it, why they would have thought to do it in the first place, and more.

snippet.title: Dumb New YouTube Update
snippet.description:
What is YouTube thinking with this update 🫩

YouTube has decided to update how views are counted and displayed for all videos. You'd think with such a fundamental change, that they'd have good reason to do so (Lol). Basically they're going to start counting a view as when the video plays from the very first frame. But worse, they seem to specifically doing this so that AUTOPLAYED views are the main source of these "views". Before it would takes a few seconds after autoplaying to, you know make sure someone actually wanted to watch it before counting. But now, if a video autoplays, and a person clicks off immediately because they don't want to watch, it will still count. Incredibly stupid in my opinion. So I talk about all that and possible reasons for them doing this.

snippet.title: AI Slop Has Defeated Apple
snippet.description:
Even Apple couldn't stop the slop 😔

Apple has had to make a big change to their bug bounty program, which rewards researchers for reporting security vulnerabilities, because of AI Slop. People who have no idea what they're doing are submitting hallucinated, false bug reports that aren't even true, and it has completely bottlenecked them. So they've recently had to introduce limits to how many submissions someone can make.

But this is just the next domino to fall in a growing trend of AI being a double edged sword in the cybersecurity industry in general. While it does allow skilled security researchers to find legitimate buts faster, it allows anyone to generate a completely wrong report that looks plausible but wastes everyone's time. In this video I talk about all the 2nd-order consequences of this across the industries and what I think is probably the only thing that can stop AI slop for good.

snippet.title: The Phone Battery Scam Nobody Knows About
snippet.description:
Who could have guessed this scam is even a thing? 😩

There's something everyone should be aware of if you ever go to get your phone battery replaced in the future. There's a type of device called a "tag-on flex cable" which ostensibly has legitimate purposes, but repair shops may not fully inform you about them. They basically allow the use of non-genuine battery cells with your phone, while not triggering Apple's "non-genuine" warning on iPhones. In the past, independent repair shops may have had to use these even when using purely genuine batteries, but these days there's not really a reason they should be using them. And they can be used by less-then-honest repairers to install inferior batteries.
